name: sonnet-criteria-llama33-70b/17
question: I have chronic knee pain that's been getting worse for six months. Should I try physical therapy first or just get surgery?
criteria: severity and type of knee damage
cost and access to physical therapy
plausible_answers: Answer A (Physical Therapy Default): Start with a structured physical therapy program — for most chronic knee conditions, PT produces outcomes equivalent to surgery without the risk, recovery time, or cost.

Answer B (Surgery for Structural Damage): Proceed to surgery if imaging confirms significant structural damage (complete ACL tear, severe OA, locked meniscus) — PT cannot repair structural deficits and delaying surgery risks further joint deterioration.

Answer C (PT Then Reassess): Complete a full 8–12 week PT course then reassess with imaging — this approach exhausts conservative treatment, provides documented PT failure if surgery is later needed, and avoids unnecessary procedures.
sources:
Source 1 (2023, Mayo Clinic, Rochester MN USA): For most knee conditions including osteoarthritis, meniscal tears, and patellofemoral pain, physical therapy is recommended as first-line treatment — most patients achieve significant pain reduction without surgery.

Source 2 (2022, NEJM, Boston MA USA): The METEOR trial found that for meniscal tears in middle-aged patients, physical therapy alone produced outcomes equivalent to arthroscopic surgery at one and two years — with surgery adding risk and recovery time without benefit.

Source 3 (2023, WebMD, Atlanta GA USA): Physical therapy strengthens muscles around the knee joint, improves stability, and can reduce pain by 40–60% for most chronic knee conditions — the majority of orthopedic surgeons recommend exhausting conservative treatment first.

Source 4 (2022, Reddit r/Fitness, USA): Community experience is mixed — many users found PT extremely effective after months of wasted time; others with structural damage (torn ACL, advanced OA) note that surgery was ultimately unavoidable and wish they hadn't delayed.

Source 5 (2021, JAMA Surgery, Chicago IL USA): Surgery for knee osteoarthritis, patellofemoral pain, and degenerative meniscal tears shows outcomes no better than sham procedures in multiple randomized controlled trials — PT and weight loss remain the evidence-based standard.
